## What it is
High-frequency (10-minute) climatological data from the D1 climate station on Niwot Ridge, Colorado (elevation ~3738 m). Part of the Niwot Ridge LTER long-term monitoring program.

## Source and access

- **EDI package ID:** `knb-lter-nwt.273`
- **Metadata page:** [https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?packageid=knb-lter-nwt.273](https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?packageid=knb-lter-nwt.273)
- **DOI (example):** [https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/e06669d42e1314dd93160d091022a717](https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/e06669d42e1314dd93160d091022a717)
- **Original README:** [Climate_2_NiwotRidge_D1_README.md](https://github.com/EAES-380/2026-Final-Project-Data-Options/blob/main/Climate_2_NiwotRidge_D1_README.md)

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Note on access (from the course README):** Most EDI datasets can be downloaded directly from the metadata page (or via the generated R/Python code). Some require a free EDI access key for scripted downloads. Check the “Accessing Data” documentation on the EDI site if you encounter authentication prompts.
:::

## Variables and contents
- Air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and direction, solar radiation
- Quality-flagged native-resolution data
- Suitable for alpine climate and meteorology studies

## Temporal & spatial coverage
- **Time:** 2014–ongoing (10-minute resolution)
- **Location:** Niwot Ridge, Colorado Front Range, USA (high-elevation alpine)

## Why this dataset is useful for final projects
Students interested in alpine or mountain meteorology can examine high-elevation climate variability, wind patterns, or radiation regimes. High temporal resolution supports diurnal cycle analyses.

## Suggested questions and analyses
- Diurnal and seasonal temperature/wind cycles
- Extreme wind or temperature events at high elevation
- Comparison with lower-elevation stations
